Type
System

From expressive headlines to compact data, maintain one consistent visual voice. Variable axes, weights, type scale, and tokens create a flexible system for brand and product experiences.

Design Space

The Variable Font covers a continuous spectrum from lightweight information to high-impact display typography. Designers may explore continuous values, while handoff should prioritize the recommended nodes.

Weights & Usage

Each weight has a clear responsibility—from supporting copy and body text to interaction labels, critical data, and expressive display headlines.

Type Scale

Display, Headline, Title, Body, and Label define five semantic roles. Large, Medium, and Small create fifteen levels; every level specifies size, line height, weight, tracking, and intended use.

Type Tokens

Semantic naming connects visual parameters to intended use. The default family is TRON Variable; each token contains size, line height, weight, and tracking.

Usage & Readability

Size, line height, weight, and line length must work together. These boundaries keep English content readable across brand communications and product interfaces.

  1. Use at least 14px for product body copy; default to 16px / 24px.
  2. Keep body line height between 1.4× and 1.6× the font size.
  3. Limit continuous text to 45–75 English characters per line.
  4. Reserve all caps for buttons, navigation, and short status labels.
  1. Do not use body text below 14px in product interfaces.
  2. Avoid line heights below 1.2× or above 1.8× the font size.
  3. Do not set long paragraphs in all caps or heavy weights.
  4. Avoid overly long lines, extreme tracking, or centered body copy.
